headline: Approved CT STEM Academy lease at 284 Washington Street, consent agenda items, and waiver of IT infrastructure bid
summary: The Council approved consent agenda items including tax refunds, a donation appropriation, a fund transfer, and a church sign replacement. It approved a 5-year lease with CT Stem Academy for a storage building at 284 Washington Street for $1.00 per year, following public comment and councilor discussion. After an executive session on a public security matter, the Council approved waiving the bid process for critical IT infrastructure.
decisions: Approved Consent Agenda items 3a through 3e, including tax refunds totaling $5,318.00, a $20 donation appropriation, a $62,500 transfer for IT salaries, and replacement of First Congregational Church's sign.
Approved a 5-year Lease Agreement with CT Stem Academy for use of a free-standing storage building at 284 Washington Street at $1.00 per year, by a vote of 6 Aye to 1 Nay.
Approved entering Executive Session under CGS Sections 1-225(f) and 1-200(6)(C) to discuss a public security matter.
Approved waiving the bid process for the purchase of critical IT infrastructure, by a vote of 5 Aye to 1 Nay.

Reynolds, Bryan Rivard, Melanie Rossacci (remote), Christina Tatta and Chairman Vincent F. Testa, Jr. 
Mayor Vincent Cervoni, Town Attorney Geoffrey Einhorn, Comptroller Tim Sena and Acting Town

 4. Items Removed from the Consent Agenda 
 
 5. PUBLIC QUESTION & ANSWER PERIOD 
 
Bill Comerford asked the Mayor about the status of the possible contaminated soil at Center Street 
Cemetery.  He stated he has an audio tape with someone saying the soil is contaminated.  Chairman 
Testa responded that he had asked for a copy of the recording at the previous meeting.  Once the audio 
recording has been provided to the Town Council, they will address the issue. 
 
Larry Kellogg asked about the status of signage for the crosswalk at the intersection of Parker Farms Rd 
and North Turnpike Rd, promised by the Wallingford Police Department in April 2026.  Chairman Testa 
apologized for not having answers and will follow up. 
 
Susan Huizenga addressed the Council as a representative of WPAA-TV and Community Media Center 
and asked for more transparency and a public process regarding the budget and handling of nonprofit 
matters. Chairman Testa stated that there are discussions for a workshop to review the process and 
encouraged Ms. Huizenga to participate and provide feedback. 
 
Sheila Tierney asked Attorney Einhorn for an update on the sidewalk inspections and procedures.  
Attorney Einhorn responded that there is no written policy in the Engineering Dept.  Chairman Testa 
expressed apologies for not having answers and will follow up.  Ms. Tierney also asked about a 
$390,000 transfer for paving, made at the June 9, 2026 Town Council meeting. She would like a list of 
the roads that have been paved this year, and which are still due to be paved. 
 
Bill Comerford asked why the Building Maintenance Dept was disbanded and would like to see it 
reinstated.  He would also like a list of catch basins that have been cleaned. 
 
Anthony Parent expressed concern over a catch basin on Lincoln Drive that has been paved over, and 
the grate cannot be removed.  We had a large storm in June, and he is concerned about small animals 
being trapped if washed into the basin by extreme water. 
 
 6. Discussion of old business – Chairman Testa 
 
(a) Discussion of status of the town contribution to the Golden Fox Theater. 
 
Chairman Testa requested an update on any potential progress regarding the Town contribution to 
Golden Fox Theater.  Mayor stated that he invited Mr. Michael to schedule a time to review financial 
information with him and help to complete his budget.  Mr. Michael responded that he was away on 
vacation and would respond to the Mayor upon his return.

7. Consider and approve a Lease Agreement between the Town of Wallingford and the CT 
Stem Academy for the use of free-standing storage building at 284 Washington Street for 
a term of 5 years, at a rental of $1.00 per year – Mayor  
 
MOTION WAS MADE TO approve a Lease Agreement between the Town of Wallingford and the 
CT Stem Academy for the use of free-standing storage building at 284 Washington Street for a 
term of 5 years, at a rental of $1.00 per year - Mayor 
 
MADE BY: CARMODY  
SECONDED BY: REYNOLDS  
 
Christopher Stone, Executive Director of CT STEM Academy, Donna Regan, Board Member CT STEM 
Academy and Doug Papallo, President of the Board CT STEM Academy addressed the Council 
regarding the renewal of the Lease.  Mayor Cervoni stated this is an enriching and confidence-building 
program that benefits the students of Wallingford. 
 
Councilor Rossacci stated that she feels the STEM Academy does great work but would like to see a 
more transparent process of deciding town resources.  She would like to focus on reducing subjectivity 
and adding objectivity. 
 
Councilor Tatta agreed with Councilor Rossacci.  After reviewing the lease, Councilor Tatta is ok with 
the town providing maintenance and normal repair but has concern over the town supplying janitorial 
services and utilities such as water, sewer, gas and electricity.  She asked what other groups are given 
notice of use of this facility or the opportunity to have use of the town facility for free.  She would like 
to see a more transparent process for others that may express their interest.  She finds it difficult to listen 
to residents talk about how they cannot pay bills and then give resources away where the town can make 
a profit.  She also questioned why these leases are not included in the budget and would like a 
comprehensive list of all contributions that the town has provided, such as Public Work hours and 
janitorial services. Siting the Charter, Councilor Tatta questioned why these leases are presented by the 
administration to the Council.  Her understanding of the Charter is that Council approves and 
administers the leases.  Attorney Einhorn stated that is not his understanding of the Charter and if 
Council submits a question to the Law Department, he will supply an opinion to the Council. Mayor 
clarified that the lease is in front of the Council for approval. This is the Council’s time to scrutinize the 
lease and the process.  The Council can deliberate and vote for or against it but the lease is before the 
Council for their approval. 
 
Christopher Stone addressed the Council.  He stated that CT Stem Academy is a nonprofit 501-3(c).  
They attain their own funding and partner with other organizations.  They are not funded by the Town of 
Wallingford and do have paid staff.  They offer programs through Wallingford Parks and Recreation 
Department and  use donations, grant funding and programming fees to reduce costs to make their 
programs accessible to anyone that wishes to participate.  They collaborate with SCOW to offer free 
programming to students in the summertime.

Councilor Reynolds asked about any renovations to the building since they have been using it 5 years 
ago.  Mr. Stone stated they added wall hangings for competitions that were won, TV’s and equipment 
for the facility such as 3-D Printers.  They are continuously looking to enhance the building without 
making permanent modifications.  Internet is being utilized with an agreement with SCOW.  Councilor 
Reynolds asked about enrollment.  Mr. Stone answered that the program registers approximately 600 
families through the Parks and Recreation Department per year.  Councilor Reynolds expressed his 
appreciation of the programs and providing a variety of options not available in sports. 
 
Councilor Rivard reviewed the lease and acknowledged the agreement has a clause that either party can 
termination the lease with 90-day written notice.  He wishes the terms of the lease were more in line 
with a Council or budgetary time-period.  He feels this would make more sense to review the leases with 
more frequency.  He supports the CT STEM Academy and feels these types of enrichment programs 
provide value to the taxpayers. 
 
Councilor Testa feels this is an organization that outgrew the schools and Wallingford was able to assist 
and provide a space so the program can continue.  He acknowledges they are not a town department or 
specifically a town organization but provides programs that benefit Wallingford residents. 
 
Councilor Laffin expressed his support for CT STEM Academy and is impressed by the growth and 
success of the program.  Wallingford provides maintenance of sports fields and outbuildings for soccer, 
football, and baseball.  We should provide building maintenance for the CT STEM Academy.  The 
programs provide opportunities to excel in STEM and future career advancement.  He feels we are a 
better community for having strong community partners.   
 
Christopher Stone thanked the Council and Mayor for placing this item on the Agenda.  Connecticut 
STEM Academy is an established program with positive community impacts rooted in youth and family 
engagement.  It began as the Young Astronaut Club and has evolved into the CT STEM Academy 
through continued partnership with Wallingford Youth and Social Services, Spanish Community of 
Wallingford (SCOW), Wallingford Parks and Recreation Department, offering low cost or free 
programs to families in need. 
 
Donna Regan added that the CT STEM Academy has provided employment opportunities to 
Wallingford youth, which in turn helps foster productive members of society. 
 
Doug Papallo stated that the program helps kids get exposed to something they may otherwise not have 
had and can put them in a direction that could result in a lucrative career in coding, engineering, etc.  
The program also gives exposure to females in male-dominated fields. 
 
Mark Britton spoke in favor of CT STEM Academy and the positive impact he has seen with his own 
children.

JD Oliveira spoke in support of CT STEM Academy.  The money put forth for services is not meant to 
have a monetary return but help to better educate children, create a collaborative work environment and 
expose children to things they may not ordinarily see.  The program offers opportunities to kids that may 
not participate in sports. 
 
Lara Juarez expressed her support for CT STEM Academy.  She is a Wallingford resident and started 
the program in middle school.  She has worked at CT STEM Academy for the past 10 years and 
currently serves as a program facilitator, community outreach coordinator and robotics director.  The 
program provides benefits for underserved Latina women.
